summary: The S&P 500 closed at 7,623.68 on Oct 23, 2.5% below its Oct 6 record (7,818.93). Underneath the index, breadth has improved sharply: 58-61% of members are above their 50-day average, 57% above the 200-day, and the equal-weight side is outperforming mega-caps. Credit is calm (HY OAS ~316bp). VIX is 19.45 and drifting higher, but the curve is still in contango (VIX9D 18.70 < VIX3M 20.48), so this is event hedging, not panic. The problem is the calendar: this week stacks the Oct 27-28 FOMC (Warsh's Fed, ~90% priced for a hold after September's hike), Microsoft/Alphabet/Meta (Oct 28), Amazon plus Q3 GDP and September PCE (Oct 29), the ECB and BoJ, and then the Nov 3 midterms and Nov 10 CPI. Hawkish Fed speakers (Williams sees one more 2026 hike) plus a hot September CPI (3.7% headline) keep a December hike live. Deploy new cash only after the FOMC/PCE and CPI hurdles clear, and favor small-cap/equal-weight leadership over crowded AI mega-caps.
